standard_prerequisites.name: The specialization relation between points and the definitions of stability under specialization and under generalization
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Set up in the author's section on specialization, immediately before the counted statement
standard_prerequisites.use: Fixes the three assertions and the relation used throughout.

core_obligations: Part (1): for a closed subset and a point of it, the closure of the singleton is contained in the subset, so every specialization of the point lies in the subset, which is stability under specialization (proof lines 3797-3799).

Part (3): the equivalence between stability under specialization of a subset and stability under generalization of its complement is proved by running the specialization relation in the reverse direction (proof lines 3800-3807).
Part (2): stability of open subsets under generalization follows from (1) and (3) by passing to the complement, as the author states (proof line 3808).
Conclusion: the three numbered assertions (proof line 3808).
proof_roadmap: (1) 若 y ∈ F 且 F 闭，则 cl{y} ⊂ F，故 y 的一切 specialization 都在 F 中。
(3) 把 specialization 关系反过来即得 T 对 specialization 稳定 ⇔ 补集对 generalization 稳定；(2) 由 (1)(3) 取补得到。
difficulty_reason: The counted statement collects the interaction of the specialization relation with closed and open subsets (author lemma at source lines 3784-3794, label lemma-open-closed-specialization): closed sets are stable under specialization, open sets under generalization, and the two stabilities are exchanged by complementation. The proof (source lines 3796-3809) is short and direct: part (1) is the containment of the closure of a singleton in a closed set, part (3) is the reversal of the relation for the complement, and part (2) is their combination (proof lines 3797-3808). The lemma is the reference point for the chapter's later results on constructible sets and on spectral spaces, where specialization-stability is used constantly. H2.
